QUOTE: The pollers and observers read a flag every 10 ms and set an atomic. ... The C ABI only ever sees `int*`, so no `std::atomic` crosses the `.so` boundary.

VERDICT: MISS

WHY: The answer says the C ABI only sees `int*`. But it describes the pollers as reading an `int*` and setting an atomic, which is the reverse of the item. It also describes the interrupt observer as mirroring the engine's flag into an `int`, without saying that this bridges an atomic into a plain int because the ABI cannot carry an atomic. It never states that this is why the observer thread exists.
